key_insight: Oxide-cap position shapes aluminum-particle combustion: front caps enhance local evaporation near the cap–metal junction, while rear caps absorb heat and lower reaction temperatures.
engineering_relevance: Cap-aware evaporation and drag models can improve Lagrangian predictions of burning aluminum particles without resolving each particle’s boundary layer.
method: Use boundary-layer-resolved simulations to vary cap size, cap orientation, and particle Reynolds number.
Approximate film conditions with a 0.55-rule and optimize Whitaker evaporation and Schiller–Naumann drag correlations.
Extend the model to capped doublet particles using exposed aluminum area and a front-cap evaporation correction.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports good agreement between optimized correlations and simulations, with exposed-area scaling predicting rear-cap evaporation well but front caps requiring an additional correction.
watch_item: Exposed-area scaling alone is insufficient for front caps, particularly at high particle Reynolds numbers; the abstract does not specify quantitative errors or validity ranges.
paper_title: Influence of an oxide cap on the combustion of aluminum particles using boundary-layer resolved simulations
